title: 2007 AMC 10B Problem 4
statement: The point \(O\) is the center of the circle circumscribed about \(\triangle ABC,\) with \(\angle BOC = 120^\circ\) and \(\angle AOB = 140^\circ,\) as shown. What is the degree measure of \(\angle ABC?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(OA=OB=OC,\) triangles \(AOB, BOC,\) and \(COA\) are isosceles. The base angles give \(\angle ABO=\dfrac{180^\circ-140^\circ}{2}=20^\circ\) and \(\angle OBC=\dfrac{180^\circ-120^\circ}{2}=30^\circ.\)

Therefore \(\angle ABC=20^\circ+30^\circ=50^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Each radius is equal, so each of the triangles \(AOB, BOC, COA\) is isosceles
\(\angle ABC=\angle ABO+\angle OBC,\) where each part is a base angle of an isosceles triangle
